name: Rodman Reservoir
type: Flooded Ocklawaha River valley: stumps, standing timber, grass, mats and the old river channel
pool: Barge Canal and river channel run to 30 ft;Drawn down about 7 ft every 3 to 4 years
notes: Coolest water. Bass stage near the spawning flats; specks school offshore.
Spawn starts on warm spells. Big bass move shallow around the moon.
Peak spawn for bass and specks around the full moon.
Post-spawn. Shellcracker spawn on the full moon.
Shad spawn at dawn; bluegill bed on the full moon.
Summer pattern: topwater early, then mats and offshore grass.
Hottest stretch. Fish first light, last light and after storms.
Hottest water. Short bites at dawn and around storms.
Shad move shallow as the nights cool.
Fall feed. Bass school on shad in creeks and canals.
Cold fronts start the speck bite offshore.
Cold fronts. Bass on outside grass; specks school in open water.

flbass.doing: Cold water bunches bass on winter structure: channel swings, bends and deep laydowns. Rodman is a trophy lake; during drawdowns FWC has made bass catch-and-release.
how: Football jig or big worm on channel swings and bends.
Shiners around deep laydowns and timber.
Check FWC for drawdown rules before keeping bass.

specks.doing: Specks suspend in the deeper water of the Barge Canal and river channel. Use your electronics to find the depth.
how: Live minnows under floats at the depth you mark.
Small plastic-tailed jigs in chartreuse, yellow or white.

bream.doing: Panfish slow down in cold weather; fish deeper stumps and pads on warm afternoons.
how: Worms on the bottom near stumps.

flbass.doing: January: pre-spawn fish stage on the old river channel, oxbow mouths and inside bends.

specks.doing: Schools leave the open water for pad fields, bulrush and Kissimmee grass that sit next to deeper water. A cold front pushes them back out.
how: Troll or drift minnow-tipped jigs along the outside of the pads and reeds.
Minnow under a cork in openings at the grass edge.
Fish the closest open water off the same grass.

bream.doing: Shellcracker move onto firm sand and shell near the grass ahead of the spring full moons; bluegill feed around reeds and docks.
how: Red wigglers on the bottom with a split shot.
Crickets or grass shrimp under a small float along reeds.

flbass.doing: February moves fish shallow into pencil reeds, pads and isolated wood in 2 to 6 ft; March is the peak shallow bite.
how: Creature baits into reeds, pads and wood.
Craw-colored lipless crankbait on hydrilla outside the spawning lanes.
Sight fish; in stained water, pitch jigs into dark spots in the pads.
Shiner under a float beside a laydown.

specks.doing: Specks spawn in pads, bulrush, cattails and Kissimmee grass over sandy bottom, in waves around the full moon, usually at about 60 to 65°F.
how: Minnow or grass shrimp under a small cork in pockets and along reed lines.
A 10 to 14 ft pole and a 1/32 to 1/16 oz jig dipped into holes in the pads.
Fish the closest deeper water off the spawning grass.

bream.doing: Shellcracker bed on the March and April full moons on firm sand and shell near grass. Bluegill start as the water warms.
how: Red wigglers on the bottom; work the area until you find the colony.
Small beetle spin along the edge of the flat.

flbass.doing: The spawn lingers into April. In May, shad spawn at daybreak on hard edges, then bass slide to shell and hard spots near river swings.
how: Prop bait or walking bait over eelgrass; vibrating jig or swim jig on the shad spawn.
Carolina rig or magnum worm on channel-edge brush and shell.

specks.doing: After the spawn, specks scatter to deeper grass edges, docks, bridges and channel edges. The bite slows as the water warms.
how: Minnows at dock pilings, bridges and fish attractors.
Small jig swum along the deep edge of the vegetation.

bream.doing: The river section from Orange Springs toward Eureka is the panfish water: bluegill, redear, redbreast and warmouth around stumps, pads and shoreline cover.
how: Stumps, pads, submerged grass and overhanging brush.

flbass.doing: Fish want shade and current: hyacinth mats, vertical wood and the shady side of big timber. The river mouth and the lock areas get feeding bursts.
how: Punch with 1 to 1.5 oz tungsten; frogs early and late.
Flip standing timber, or fish shiners on its shady side.
Big worms on the channel edges.
Spinnerbait when an afternoon storm hits.

specks.doing: The slowest season. Specks suspend in the deepest water, on fish attractors and in shade; fish early, late or at night.
how: Lights and minnows at bridges and deep docks.
Vertical jig or minnow at the depth you mark.

bream.doing: Bluegill keep spawning on each full moon; between moons they hold in deeper pads, grass patches and around docks. Fish early.
how: Grass shrimp in deep pads and hydrilla patches; anchor and chum lightly.
Worms and crickets along the walkways.

flbass.doing: Young shad gather on the backs of runs and oxbows in September; October is the fall feed on wind-blown eelgrass and points; November moves bass back toward the channel.
how: Squarebill, small walking bait or finesse swimbait.
Vibrating jig and lipless crankbait in wind-blown eelgrass lanes.
Jerkbait or lipless crankbait on outside grass; jig on hard breaks; shiners near deep timber.

specks.doing: As it cools, specks gather in the Barge Canal and river channel and along the timber edges.
how: Find suspended fish, then set baits at that depth.
Small jigs or minnows under floats.

bream.doing: Bream feed hard in the grass as the water cools. Fewer beds, steady numbers.
how: Anchor near a thick hydrilla patch and fish grass shrimp or worms near the bottom.
Crickets under a cork along reed lines.
